title: Representation Dimension of Some Finite Groups
abstractText: For a finite group G, the representation dimension is the minimal degree of a complex faithful representation of G. In this article, we compute representation dimension for some finite p-groups, in particular, for all p-groups of order up to p 5 , their direct products, and groups with certain conditions on nonlinear irreducible characters. We also compute the minimal degree of a complex faithful irreducible representation of such groups, if one exists. In the appendix, we present GAP codes to compute these numbers.

title: Classifying the surface-knot modules
abstractText: The kth module of a surface-knot of a genus g in the 4-sphere is the kth integral homology module of the infinite cyclic covering of the surface-knot complement. The reduced first module is the quotient module of the first module by the finite sub-module defining the torsion linking. It is shown that the reduced first module for every genus g is characterized in terms of properties of a finitely generated module. As a by-product, a concrete example of the fundamental group of a surface-knot of genus g which is not the fundamental group of any surface-knot of genus g − 1 is given for every g > 0. The torsion part and the torsion-free part of the second module are determined by the reduced first module and the genus-class on the reduced first module. The third module vanishes. The concept of an exact leaf of a surface-knot is introduced, whose linking is an orthogonal sum of the torsion linking and a hyperbolic linking.

title: A Divergence-Free Parametric Finite Element Method for 3D Stokes Equations on Curved Domains
abstractText: The Stokes equations play an important role in the incompressible flow simulation. In this paper, a novel divergence-free parametric mixed finite element method is proposed for solving three-dimensional Stokes equations on domains with piecewise smooth boundaries. The flow velocity and pressure are discretized with high-order parametric Brezzi-Douglas-Marini elements and volume elements, respectively, on curved tetrahedral meshes. Utilizing the interior-penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) technique, we prove the inf-sup condition for the mixed finite element pair, and high-order optimal error estimates in the energy norm, with the help of the extension and transformation of the true solution to computational domain. Moreover, the discrete velocity is exactly divergence-free, meaning that $\operatorname{div}\boldsymbol{u}_h = 0$ holds in the curved computational domain. Numerical experiments are conducted to support the theoretical analyses.

title: Time integration of quantized tensor trains using the interpolative dynamical low-rank approximation
abstractText: Quantized tensor trains (QTTs) are a low-rank and multiscale framework that allows for efficient approximation and manipulation of multi-dimensional, high resolution data. One area of active research is their use in numerical simulation of hyperbolic systems such as the Navier-Stokes equations and the Vlasov equations. One popular time integration scheme is the dynamical low-rank approximation (DLRA), in which the time integration is constrained to a low-rank manifold. However, until recently, DLRA has typically used orthogonal projectors to project the original dynamical system into a reduced space, which is only well-suited for linear systems. DLRA has also mostly been investigated in the context of non-quantized tensor trains. This work investigates interpolative DLRA schemes in which the low-rank manifold is constructed from aptly chosen interpolation points and interpolating polynomials, in the context of QTTs. Through various examples, its performance is compared to its orthogonal counterpart. This work demonstrates how interpolative DLRA is suitable for nonlinear systems and time integrators requiring nonlinear element-wise operations, such as upwind time integration schemes.

title: A Gradient Boosting-Based Machine Learning Model for the Prediction of the Hardness of Thermoplastic Polymers
abstractText: Abstract Modern experimental techniques can measure the hardness of thin films and structural features on the nanometer scale. These techniques can be applied to many types of materials, but as the hardness of the material decreases, more specialized and precise equipment is needed. For polymers, this analysis can be relatively expensive and time-consuming, so here we demonstrate a gradient-boosting-based machine-learning model that can provide a fast and reliable prediction of the hardness of thermoplastic polymers. This model is based on the XGBoost algorithm and shows reasonably good performance with an R2 value of 0.46–0.69. The features used in this study include experimental (mechanical and thermal properties) and molecular descriptors obtained using RDKit. The model is robust, with reasonable performance obtained when key experimental features are removed and/or when the selection of polymers is reduced. This suggests that this approach will be useful in “bottom-up” strategies for polymeric materials development.

title: Experience affects novel object aversion and the use of human cues in rural and urban American crows
abstractText: Abstract Population differences in behavior can result from experience, which can be drastically different between environments such as urban and rural areas. Urban areas may be more complex, contain more human-made objects but fewer natural objects, or have more non-threatening people. Consequently, animals in urban and rural populations may differ in neophobia levels, what is novel, and attention to human behavior. We conducted two experiments with a common urban bird, the American crow (Corvus brachyrhynchos). On home territories of urban and rural crow family groups, we presented objects that were either equally novel in both environments or more common in one environment than the other. Separately, we measured flight initiation distance (FID) from an approaching person using either a direct or averted, less threatening gaze for individual crows across an urban gradient. We found that urban crows were more neophobic than rural crows, as measured by the probability of feeding near an object that is equally novel in both environments. There were no differences in approach and feeding latencies for the least neophobic family member. Both urban and rural crows were less averse to objects that were more common in their respective environments. In the FID experiment, crows in highly urbanized areas had FIDs 25 m shorter for an indirect gaze, while rural crow FIDs were unaffected by gaze. FIDs were best predicted by crows’ experiences with people in a relatively large area around each trial. These results highlight how experience must be accounted for when considering population differences in behavior.

title: High-Efficiency Solar-Piezo Hybrid Energy Harvester for Long-Term Autonomous Operation of Smart Agriculture Sensor Nodes
abstractText: The paper presents the design and consideration of a highly efficient hybrid energy harvesting system, combined solar and piezo energy harvesting components to power autonomous wireless sensor nodes (WSNs) used in smart agriculture. The most important goal is to provide a maintenance free, long term operation of the sensor nodes in the envisioned variable conditions of environment. The suggested system consists of a monocrystalline solar panel and piezoelectric transducers that allow to focus both ambient light and mechanics vibrations. In-order to get maximum energy extraction, intelligent maximum power point tracking (MPPT) based power conditioning circuit is implemented, and the energy generated is stored using hybrid supercapacitor-Li-ion battery system. Up to the area of evaluation of the performance of the designed system in the real conditions, a particular WSN platform was created and deployed both in a greenhouse and an open field setting. The experimental output shows that the hybrid energy harvester records a 30-45 percent rise in energy capture than the solar-only systems. Moreover, efficiency of conversion of power is increased by about 22 % by using the MPPT implementation. The sensor nodes exhibited an outstanding reliability, surpassing 98 per cent of uptime in a 30-day non-stop deployment, and over 12 hours working autonomously without any illumination. The innovation in this study is the strength of the energy harvesting system, where supplementary sources are also utilized to increase the resilience and extend the operation weeks of smart agriculture WSNs, considering the shortcomings of using single sources in the uncontrollable outdoor situations.

title: Machine learning detection of small Strombolian eruptions in noisy multi-temporal infrared images: Toward continuous monitoring
abstractText: Abstract We show that a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on denoised multi-temporal infrared images (single images whose red, green, and blue channels hold three consecutive frames so that change between them appears as color) can detect small Strombolian eruptions that previously fell below the detection limits of conventional automated methods. Strombolian eruptions at Mount Erebus, Antarctica, range from large eruptions that eject lava throughout the crater to small eruptions that are mostly contained within the lake. We built these images from thermal imagery of the Ray lava lake and trained a CNN to classify them into three categories: “no eruption”, “small eruption”, and “large eruption”. A training and verification dataset of more than 54,000 images was built through a three-stage process, Clean → Expanded → Denoised, starting from a curated set of eruptions. We applied confident learning (Cleanlab) with five iterations of five-fold Stratified Group K-Fold cross-validation. On the held-out test set, the denoised model achieved a macro F1 of 0.9782, Matthews Correlation Coefficient = 0.9397, and macro AUC = 0.9981. To test temporal generalization, we applied the model to all December 2015 images, recorded over 10 months after the latest training images, during which the lake’s morphology changed. The network detected 49 large and 420 small eruptions. Manual verification of all detections and 2,461 stratified-sampled “no eruption” frames confirmed per-class precision of 0.98 for “large eruption” and 0.97 for “small eruption”, with a population-weighted macro F1 of 0.93.

title: Comparative analysis of graph-based metabolic network representations using graph Kernels
abstractText: Background: Metabolism comprises a series of interconnected chemical reactions, forming a complex network that can be naturally represented as a graph. In this paper, we investigate the expressive power of three graph-based representations of metabolic networks: Abstract Metabolic Networks (AMNs), metabolic Directed Acyclic Graphs (m-DAGs), and Reaction Graphs (RGs). These representations provide a hierarchical view of metabolism, with AMNs being the most abstract, m-DAGs representing an intermediate level of detail, and RGs offering the most fine-grained view. Results: Using a comprehensive set of species from the KEGG database, we construct their metabolic networks with all three representations (i.e., AMN, m-DAG, and RG), resulting in three corresponding datasets. We apply topological analyses to highlight the distinct characteristics of the three datasets and conduct a series of metabolic network comparison tests using five selected graph kernels. The conducted experiments empirically show that, although RGs provide the highest level of detail, their expressiveness is comparable to, and in some cases slightly lower than, that of m-DAGs. AMNs, while less expressive overall, perform comparably to m-DAGs and RGs when comparing organisms from very distant taxonomic groups or those adapted to different environments, suggesting that coarse-grained representations can still capture key metabolic differences under certain conditions. Conclusions: The conducted tests empirically demonstrate the effectiveness of all three representations and the relevance of the chosen kernels for comparing metabolic networks. Additionally, these findings could serve as a useful baseline reference for exploring representation and kernel choices in metagenomic or metatranscriptomic datasets derived, e.g., from environmental samples.

title: Pengaruh Kompetensi Karyawan dan Disiplin Kerja terhadap Kinerja Karyawan pada PT Idea Five Indonesia Design Engineers & Associates Jakarta Pusat
abstractText: Employee performance is a critical determinant of an organization's success in achieving its strategic objectives. This study aims to investigate the individual and simultaneous effects of Employee Competence and Work Discipline on Employee Performance at PT Idea Five Indonesia Design Engineers & Associates, Central Jakarta. Utilizing a quantitative approach, this research applies a multiple linear regression analysis model. The sampling design employs a probability sampling approach through a simple random sampling method. The study's baseline population consists of 70 employees, which was subsequently calculated using the Slovin formula at a 5% precision level, resulting in a definitive sample size of 60 respondents. Data collection was conducted by distributing questionnaires to the respondents. The results of the data analysis indicate that, partially, Employee Competence exerts a positive and significant effect on Employee Performance. Similarly, Work Discipline is partially proven to have a positive and significant effect on Employee Performance. Simultaneously, Employee Competence and Work Discipline significantly influence Employee Performance at PT Idea Five Design Indonesia Engineers & Associates, Central Jakarta. Based on the coefficient of determination), the independent variables contribute 61.6% to the variance of the dependent variable, while the remaining 38.4% is influenced by other factors outside the scope of this model.

title: Single Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution Using Multi-scale Cross-spectral Transformer Network
abstractText: Hyperspectral image super-resolution seeks to produce images with finer spatial detail while keeping spectral information consistent, which supports more reliable analysis in hyperspectral imaging applications. However, existing methods mainly rely on 2D/3D convolutions, which are limited to modeling local spatial-spectral representations and fail to fully capture global spectral dependencies across bands. To address this limitation, we develop a Multi-scale Cross-spectral Transformer Network, named MCTNet. For local representation learning, MCTNet introduces a position-guided multi-scale attention fusion module. This module combines spatial feature extraction and channel attention. It extracts contextual information at multiple scales and highlights informative spectral changes. For global representation learning, CSTM applies cross-spectral self-attention to model dependencies between distant latent spectral-dimension feature channels. Experiments on standard benchmark datasets demonstrate that MCTNet provides reconstruction accuracy and visual quality that are comparable to or better than those of recent state-of-the-art approaches.

Human Skeleton of Kuragala in Sri Lanka; based on Cultural Deposit in mid-Holocene
abstractText: This research examines the human skeletal remains discovered at Kuragala, an important archaeological site associated with prehistoric human occupation in Sri Lanka. The skeletal remains were recovered through systematic archaeological excavation conducted within a stratified cave context. Careful excavation methods, including controlled stratigraphic removal of sediments, hand sorting, and wet sieving, were employed to ensure the recovery of both skeletal and associated faunal remains. The recovered bones were analyzed using standard osteological methods to determine the biological profile of the individual, including age at death, sex, and possible pathological conditions. The skeletal remains were also examined within their archaeological context, including associated lithic artifacts, faunal assemblages, and charcoal deposits. The findings contribute to a better understanding of prehistoric populations in the region and provide valuable information regarding human biology, cultural practices, and site use within the broader framework of Sri Lanka’s prehistoric archaeological record.

abstractText: The development of multimedia technology provides opportunities for teachers to deliver learning materials in a more engaging and interactive manner. However, its utilization in elementary schools remains limited, including at SDN Semolowaru IV Surabaya, which affects the quality of instructional material delivery. This community service activity aimed to enhance teachers’ competencies in developing multimedia-based learning media through training on the use of VideoScribe as a whiteboard animation tool. The program was implemented through a series of activities consisting of socialization, demonstrations, hands-on video production practice, mentoring, and evaluation. A total of 20 teachers participated in the training and were provided with a training module as a guide for further implementation. The results indicated that 87.5% of participants considered the training highly beneficial and easy to apply in classroom learning, while most participants found the materials and training methods easy to understand. The activity successfully improved teachers’ skills in producing multimedia-based learning videos and encouraged the adoption of digital learning media. These findings demonstrate that VideoScribe can serve as an effective alternative instructional medium that supports the development of more engaging learning materials and contributes to improving the quality of education in the digital era.

title: Performance of latest-generation large language models on endodontic specialty examination questions: a comparative cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Background This study aimed to compare the performance of Gemini 3 Pro, Gemini 3 Flash, ChatGPT 5.2, and DeepSeek V3.2 on the Endodontics section of the Turkish Dental Specialty Exam (DUS), with particular attention to question source, type, and endodontic subtopic. Methods The dataset comprised 187 endodontic questions from 2012–2025, stratified into internet-sourced from 2012–2021 ( n = 127) and textbook-sourced from 2022–2025 ( n = 60). Questions were further categorized by type as case analysis, literature knowledge, combination or visual analysis, and by 10 endodontic subtopics. Following a standardized zero-shot prompting protocol (public web interfaces, default settings, single run per item), two independent endodontic assessors scored responses on a blinded 0–3 rubric, and then the two evaluator scores were averaged for each response. Overall model performance was expressed as a percentage of the maximum possible rubric score (100%). Statistical analysis employed the Friedman test, Wilcoxon Signed-Rank tests with Bonferroni correction, Mann–Whitney U and Kruskal–Wallis tests. Results All reported percentages represent normalized rubric-based performance scores, evaluating both answer selection and reasoning quality, rather than simple correct/incorrect accuracy rates. High inter-rater agreement was achieved, with quadratic weighted kappa values ranging from 0.954 to 0.998. In overall performance, Gemini 3 Pro (90.37%) and Gemini 3 Flash (88.32%) significantly outperformed ChatGPT 5.2 (78.25%) and DeepSeek V3.2 (62.12%) (adjusted p ≤ 0.001; Kendall’s W = 0.214); corresponding answer accuracies were 94.1%, 93.0%, 86.6%, and 73.3%. No significant difference was found between the Gemini models (adjusted p = 1.000). No significant difference was observed between internet-sourced and textbook-sourced questions within any model. In literature knowledge questions, combination questions, and selected endodontic subtopics, the Gemini models generally showed higher rubric-based performance than the other models. Conclusions The findings indicate high rubric-based performance of the latest-generation LLMs, particularly the Gemini 3 series, on Turkish endodontics residency examination questions. No significant difference in performance was observed between internet-sourced and textbook-sourced questions; however, contamination of the data in both groups cannot be excluded. These models may serve as adjunctive tools in endodontic education; however, examination performance does not establish clinical diagnostic performance, and their outputs require expert validation.

title: Locomotive dysfunction and spinopelvic sagittal alignment in relation to falls and stumbling in community-dwelling adults: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Falls and stumbling are commonly analyzed as a single outcome, although only falls cause injury and the two events may have different correlates. We examined both in 531 adults from the 2021 Iwaki Health Promotion Project who answered separate questions about falls and stumbling and underwent standing full-spine lateral radiography. Logistic regression models included age, sex, skeletal muscle index, sleep medication use, the 25-question Geriatric Locomotive Function Scale (GLFS-25), and one spinopelvic sagittal parameter. Overall, 83 participants (15.6%) reported a fall, 165 (31.1%) stumbling, and 188 (35.4%) either event. GLFS-25 was associated with all outcomes in every age stratum: the adjusted odds ratio per point was 1.095 (95% CI 1.055–1.137) for either event and 1.062 (1.028–1.098) for falls alone. Removing its two anxiety items reduced the area under the curve only from 0.702 to 0.682. Sagittal alignment was significantly associated only with stumbling: a smaller sagittal vertical axis in participants aged < 65 years and a larger T1 pelvic angle in those aged ≥ 65 years. However, multinomial regression did not distinguish its associations with stumbling and falls. Locomotive dysfunction was associated with both events and can be assessed without equipment, whereas the radiographic findings should be considered hypothesis-generating.

Longitudinal associations of hormone therapy and depressive symptoms in cognitively unimpaired older women
abstractText: Abstract Background Women are disproportionately affected by depressive disorders relative to men, and mid-life differences like menopause can exacerbate symptoms. Hormone therapy (HT) is a common treatment to ease menopause transitions, including vasomotor and depressive symptoms, that may occur due to menopause-related hormonal changes, but its effects on later-life depressive symptoms remain unclear. Our objective was to examine the association between self-reported post-menopausal HT use and longitudinal changes in depressive symptoms in cognitively unimpaired age-matched older men and women from the Harvard Aging Brain Study and affiliated studies, along with sub-analyses examining interactions with Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) risk factors and neuroimaging markers. Methods Linear mixed-effect models examined the relationship between HT use and changes in the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS). Secondary analyses tested the moderating effects of apolipoprotein ε4 ( APOE ε4) status, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), amyloid-β (Aβ) status, medial temporal lobe tau, and hippocampal volume on the association between HT and GDS scores over time. Results In a sample of 585 individuals (58.3% women, Age = 71.6 (+ 7.72 SD)), 42% of women reported current or past HT use. 7% of women self-reported mild to moderate depressive symptoms at baseline (GDS = 11–19). Female HT users reported significantly greater depressive symptoms over time relative to age-matched men (β = 0.11; 95% CI:-0.22- -0.01; p = 0.03) even after adjusting for history of depressive episodes, but not different relatively to female non-users (β=-0.10; 95% CI:-0.21- 0.01; p = 0.07). WMH volume moderated the relationship between HT use and changing depressive symptoms, with female HT users reported greater depressive symptoms over time relative to men (β=-0.09; 95% CI:-0.18- -0.01; p = 0.03) in the setting of high WMH volume, but not relative to female non-users (β=-0.06; 95% CI:-0.15–0.04; p = 0.28). Moderating effects of Aβ, medial temporal lobe tau, and hippocampal volume were not significant. Conclusions In the overall group, female HT users and female non-users did not differ in changes in depression scores. However, female HT users exhibited subtly greater depressive symptoms over time relative to men and WMH moderated this relationship. This underscores the importance of investigating menopausal treatment factors that may affect depressive symptoms in older women and to understand their relationship with white matter lesions.

A Multi-Scale SEIR Model with Within-Host Viral Dynamics and Fractional Memory
abstractText: We develop a multi-scale SEIR framework coupling representative within-host profiles to age- and strain-structured transmission through infectious stages. Occupancy-weighted coefficients preserve expected cumulative infectiousness along a sequential infectious path. The population model incorporates vaccination, breakthrough infections, strain switching and waning immunity. We prove global well-posedness and population conservation, and derive invasion thresholds for autonomous reference configurations. A reanalysis of the Atangana strength number shows that its minimal exposed-infectious subsystem has real characteristic roots and admits no damped oscillatory regime under nonnegative transmission. A separate Caputo surrogate is locally well posed in a continuous Volterra formulation. The interpretation of epidemic trajectories distinguishes compartment stocks, transition flows, cumulative events and peak regularity. The results clarify which conclusions follow from the stage model, its reduced subsystems and the fractional surrogate.

title: Dual-threshold graded desaturation protection for IGBTs in VSC-HVDC converter valve submodules
abstractText: Abstract A dual-threshold graded desaturation protection strategy is proposed to address differences in the short-circuit current evolution and protection requirements of insulated-gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) under different short-circuit conditions in converter valve submodules for voltage-source-converter-based high-voltage direct-current (VSC-HVDC) transmission. The high-threshold channel uses independently configured detection-circuit parameters and a shortened blanking time to provide fast protection under low-inductance short-circuit conditions. The low-threshold channel uses a trip level determined from the device output characteristics and requires the detection voltage to remain above this level for a specified duration to identify slowly rising overcurrents under high-inductance short-circuit conditions. A first-order dynamic model of the detection voltage is established to derive coordination constraints among the detection threshold, response time constant, and confirmation delay. Experiments are conducted for three protection configurations: conventional high-threshold protection, optimized high-threshold protection, and low-threshold protection. The results show that the optimized high-threshold protection reduces the protection operating time by approximately 47% compared with the conventional scheme, while the low-threshold protection effectively clears faults during slowly rising overcurrent conditions.

title: Investigation on Switching Characteristics of Multiple Pulse States in a Dual-Wavelength Bismuth-Doped Fiber Laser
abstractText: Abstract We demonstrate four switchable pulse states at 1.3 μm in a dual-wavelength bismuth-doped fiber laser based on nonlinear polarization rotation. By adjusting the pump power and polarization, we achieve four switchable pulse states: mode-locking, breathing, Q-switching, and Q-switched mode-locking. All states are dual-wavelength, operating at 1362 nm and 1426–1431 nm with a separation of 63–69 nm. The laser delivers a fundamental repetition rate of 1.71 MHz. At the breathing-pulse state, the pulse envelope undergoes periodic modulation with a characteristic period of 50 μs, whereas the Q-switching state operates at a repetition rate of 21.0 kHz. The Q-switched mode-locked envelope amplitude is continuously tunable via polarization.

Management Anesthesia of Lumbar Plexus Block and Sacral Plexus Block for Hip Disarticulation Due to ALI Rutherford IIB with Severe Cardiac and Pulmonary Problems
abstractText: Background : Acute limb ischemia (ALI) is a vascular emergency associated with a high risk for limb loss and death. Peripheral artery disease is responsible for 12 to 15% of deaths in Europe. The spectrum ranges from asymptomatic or intermittent claudication to necrosis and limb loss2. Case Illustration : A 68 year old man with a diagnosis of Rutherford IIB acute limb ischemia (ALI) in the left leg presented with complaints of blackening extending to the upper lower extremity. The patient was admitted to the cardiac HCU with a diagnosis of low EF 24%, severe segmental kinetic disorder, LV apical thrombus, LV sec, grade 3 pulmonary edema, pulmonary consolidation sinistra, pneumonia dextra and sepsis. The patient was scheduled for left hip disarticulation. Anesthesia management involved a lumbar plexus block with isobaric bupivacaine 0.5% 20 mL (100 mg) and a sacral plexus block with isobaric bupivacaine 0.5% 15 mL (75 mg). After the hip disarticulation procedure, the patient desaturation until 88%, suplementation oksigen with non rebreathing mask (NRM) at 15 lpm, improving to 95%. The patient was admitted to the ICU. In the ICU, the saturation was 90% with NRM at 15 lpm, so non invasive ventilation (NIV) was used with a pressure support of 5, PEEP of 5 and FiO2 of 100%. The patient also hypoglycemia (23 g/dl). After evaluation with GDS and weaning off NIV, the patient was transferred to the ward with a Numeric Rating Score (NRS) of 1-2. Conclusion : The operation lasted for 3 hours with no pain during the procedure and stable vital signs monitoring. Pain evaluation after the operation showed a score of 1-2 using the Numeric Rating Score (NRS).

title: Identifying implementation research priorities for the ENAP (Every Newborn Action Plan) and EPMM (Ending Preventable Maternal Mortality) networks: mixed-methods study in six Asian countries
abstractText: Abstract Background The ENAP and EPMM, now unified as Every Woman Every Newborn Everywhere (ENEW), are multi-partner and multi-country networks to end preventable maternal, neonatal mortality, morbidity, and stillbirth, primarily led by United Nations agencies. Several authors promote implementation research (IR) as a key step in adapting maternal-newborn health (MNH) strategies and programmes to different contexts. This study aimed to identify key interventions requiring further IR to improve MNH with high quality of care (QoC) in six Asian countries within the ENAP/EPMM networks by combining data from a literature review and implementers’ opinions. Methods Six countries were selected based on predefined criteria. The study employed a multistep process. First, MNH data and national key documents related to MNH and targets were assessed to understand the country’s health situation and potential policy gaps in promoting high QoC. In parallel, a scoping literature review of MNH care in each country identified, through an inductive qualitative analysis, preliminary key interventions for MNH that require further IR. These were subsequently validated through key stakeholder interviews. Results Based on the document review, all countries were far from reaching the ENAP/EPMM 2030 goals, except for the Philippines. The literature review screened 780 articles and included 356 from all countries, which identified the preliminary IR priorities. After the result validation with stakeholders, several strategies for MNH, shared by more than one country, were identified for further IR as interventions to 1) improve workforce competencies, like employing mobile health (mHealth) technologies, and 2) increase equity in access to care with Community Health Worker (CHW) programmes, which were also helpful in facilitating other IR priorities. Additional IR priorities included interventions to promote 3) respectful maternal care, 4) maternal psychological well-being, 5) contraception access, 6) institutional care with community awareness and husband inclusion in MNH care, 7) malpractice prevention, and 8) caesarean section regulation. Conclusion Identified key interventions for MNH requiring further IR can inform researchers and policymakers. The study provides a model for identifying IR priorities, combining evidence reviews with the perspectives of key implementers.

Ghost Pharmacists in the Philippines: A Critical Analysis of Professional Accountability, Patient Safety, and Leadership
abstractText: Ghost pharmacist practice in the Philippines presents ethical, professional, regulatory, and leadership concerns because the use of a pharmacist’s credentials without genuine professional presence creates a gap between formal regulatory compliance and actual professional responsibility. The primary objective of this critical analysis is to examine ethical and professional issues, stakeholder responsibilities, leadership response, patient access and regulatory enforcement, potential root causes, professional accountability, and public trust. Institutional Theory, Professional Ethics Theory, and Systems Theory provide complementary lenses for examining the institutional, professional, organizational, and systemic dimensions of the practice. The analysis indicates that ghost pharmacist practice cannot be adequately examined as individual misconduct alone, as organizational practices, regulatory oversight, commercial pressures, and professional conditions may also influence its persistence. However, these factors should not be interpreted as direct causes where empirical evidence is limited. Professional accountability extends to pharmacists and to organizations responsible for pharmacy operations, while regulatory authorities have responsibilities for effective oversight and enforcement. Appropriate responses require evidence-based investigation, due process, and proportionate enforcement while protecting legitimate patient access to medicines. Genuine pharmacist presence, appropriate staffing, organizational safeguards, confidential reporting, and consistent regulatory oversight may strengthen professional accountability and reduce opportunities for nominal compliance. Addressing ghost pharmacist practice therefore requires coordinated responses across professional, organizational, institutional, and system levels, with patient welfare as the primary consideration in pharmacy practice, leadership, and regulatory decision-making.

Pengaruh Program Flashsale dan Gratis Ongkir Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Konsumen di Platform Shopee Bagi Generasi Z di Wilayah Cengkareng
abstractText: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh semakin ketatnya persaingan antar platform e-commerce di Indonesia, sehingga Shopee menerapkan berbagai strategi promosi seperti program flash sale dan gratis ongkir untuk menarik minat konsumen, khususnya Generasi Z. Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk menganalisis pengaruh program flash sale dan gratis ongkir terhadap keputusan pembelian pada platform Shopee bagi Gen Z di wilayah Cengkareng. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan pendekatan deskriptif dan verifikatif. Teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan purposive sampling dengan jumlah responden sebanyak 47 orang yang merupakan Generasi Z di wilayah Cengkareng dan pernah berbelanja di Shopee. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui penyebaran kuesioner menggunakan skala Likert, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji validitas, uji reliabilitas, uji asumsi klasik, analisis regresi linear berganda, uji t, uji F, dan koefisien determinasi dengan bantuan program IBM SPSS Statistics 27. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa program flash sale dan gratis ongkir secara parsial maupun simultan berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Variabel gratis ongkir memiliki pengaruh yang lebih dominan dibandingkan program flash sale. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa strategi promosi yang memberikan manfaat ekonomi secara langsung mampu meningkatkan keputusan pembelian konsumen Generasi Z pada platform Shopee. This research is motivated by the increasingly intense competition among e-commerce platforms in Indonesia, encouraging Shopee to implement various promotional strategies, such as flash sale and free shipping, to attract consumers, especially Generation Z. The purpose of this study is to analyze the effect of flash sale and free shipping programs on purchasing decisions among Generation Z in the Cengkareng area who shop on Shopee. This study employed a quantitative method with descriptive and verificative approaches. The sampling technique used was purposive sampling, involving 47 respondents who belong to Generation Z, reside in Cengkareng, and have previously made purchases through Shopee. Data were collected using a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed through validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, t-test, F-test, and coefficient of determination using IBM SPSS Statistics 27. The findings indicate that both flash sale and free shipping programs have a positive and significant effect, both partially and simultaneously, on purchasing decisions. Furthermore, the free shipping program has a more dominant influence than the flash sale program. These findings suggest that promotional strategies providing direct economic benefits can effectively encourage purchasing decisions among Generation Z consumers on the Shopee platform.

title: Short- and Mid-Term Clinical, Functional, and Radiographic Outcomes of the 5C® MEDic Knee System Following Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty
abstractText: Background Medial pivot total knee arthroplasty (TKA) has been developed to better reproduce native knee kinematics and improve patient satisfaction compared with conventional implant designs. This study evaluated the short- and mid-term clinical, functional, radiographic, and survivorship outcomes of the 5C® MEDic medial pivot knee system following primary TKA. Methods A retrospective cohort study included 419 primary TKAs performed in 372 patients between 2022 and 2025, with a minimum follow-up of 12 months. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS-12), Oxford Knee Score (OKS), Forgotten Joint Score (FJS-12), visual analogue scale (VAS) satisfaction, and range of motion. Radiographic evaluation included hip–knee–ankle angle, arithmetic HKA, joint line obliquity, lateral distal femoral angle, medial proximal tibial angle, and Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee (CPAK) classification. Implant survivorship was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis. Results Significant improvements were observed in all patient-reported outcome measures at 1 year . Mean OKS improved from 20.8 preoperatively to 41.2, while KOOS subscales demonstrated substantial gains in pain, symptoms, function, sports, and quality of life. Knee flexion increased from 111.1° to 123.2°, and extension improved from −5.6° to −0.7°. Kaplan–Meier survivorship was 99.8% at 1 year. One acute periprosthetic joint infection was successfully treated with debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention, and one patient developed deep venous thrombosis. No cases of aseptic loosening, instability, mechanical failure, or periprosthetic fracture were observed. Conclusions The 5C® MEDic medial pivot knee system demonstrated excellent early clinical, functional, and radiographic outcomes, high patient satisfaction, a low complication rate, and excellent short- and mid- term survivorship following primary TKA.

title: EMO-FlexNet: A Domain-Aware and Explainable Multimodal Fusion Framework for Emotion Recognition
abstractText: Emotion recognition plays a vital role in affective computing but faces challenges like noisy data, incomplete feature extraction, and limited cross-modal adaptability. Existing multimodal models often struggle to balance accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability across diverse real-world scenarios. This paper proposed an advanced multimodal emotion recognition framework, Emotion-Aware Flexible Network for Multimodal Fusion (EMO-FlexNet), designed for efficiency, interpretability, and domain-awareness. A domain-specific BERT model is pretrained on emotion-centric corpora to better capture affective cues in text. For audio, a refined Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) is employed, enhanced through emotion-domain pretraining, multi-scale spectrogram input, and fusion of prosodic features. Visual features are extracted using a Depthwise Separable Convolution-based ResNet, significantly reducing computational overhead while maintaining expressive power for facial emotion representation. Cross-modal attention mechanisms are used to capture interdependencies across modalities, and Multimodal Compact Bilinear Pooling (MCB) facilitates efficient feature fusion. To promote model transparency, SHAP and Grad-CAM are incorporated for explainability. To optimize hyperparameters and fusion weights effectively, the Adaptive Cheetah Optimization Algorithm (AChOA) is integrated, enhancing model convergence and robustness. AChOA performance is compared against existing metaheuristics such as Crocodile Optimization Algorithm (CrOA), Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO). Comparative evaluations on benchmark MELD datasets demonstrate that the proposed EMO-FlexNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods, including TRAVENet, MultiEmotionNet, EfficientNet, and TCN, in accuracy, robustness, and interpretability, making it ideal for affective computing and empathetic AI applications.

Regional-Scale Object Feature Recognition in High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images Based on YOLOv8
abstractText: Accurate object detection in regional-scale remote sensing imagery is challenged by significant scale variation, dense small targets, and complex background interference. While mainstream detection frameworks have achieved competitive results, their performance often declines when directly applied to high-resolution aerial scenes. To address this issue, this paper presents an enhanced YOLOv8-based detection framework and conducts a systematic comparative evaluation against representative state-of-the-art methods. A lightweight attention-guided multi-scale feature refinement module is introduced to strengthen small object representation, and an optimized feature aggregation strategy is adopted to improve localization precision without increasing computational complexity. Experiments are performed on two widely used remote sensing datasets, NWPU VHR-10 and DIOR. The proposed method achieves consistent performance improvements over competitive mainstream detectors, with approximately 1.98% gain in mAP while preserving real-time efficiency. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the proposed refinement mechanism. The results demonstrate that the improved YOLOv8 framework provides a robust and efficient solution for regional-scale remote sensing object detection.

title: Strategi Komunikasi Pemasaran Eiger Lhokseumawe Melalui Instagram Dalam Membangun Brand Awareness di Kalangan Mahasiswa Universitas Malikussaleh
abstractText: Perkembangan Instagram sebagai media komunikasi pemasaran digital mendorong pelaku usaha lokal memanfaatkan platform tersebut untuk membangun kesadaran merek. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengetahui dan mendeskripsikan strategi komunikasi pemasaran EIGER Lhokseumawe melalui Instagram dalam membangun brand awareness di kalangan mahasiswa Universitas Malikussaleh. Pendekatan yang digunakan adalah kualitatif dengan teknik purposive sampling terhadap enam informan, yaitu tiga pihak internal EIGER Lhokseumawe dan tiga mahasiswa pengguna aktif Instagram. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi nonpartisipan, wawancara semi-terstruktur, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis melalui tahapan reduksi data, penyajian data, serta penarikan kesimpulan dengan triangulasi teknik dan sumber. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa EIGER Lhokseumawe menerapkan strategi Integrated Marketing Communication melalui periklanan, promosi penjualan, hubungan masyarakat, pemasaran interaktif, dan word of mouth. Periklanan disampaikan melalui foto, video, Reels, dan Highlight; promosi penjualan melalui informasi diskon dan program Buy More, Save More; hubungan masyarakat melalui penguatan citra merek outdoor; pemasaran interaktif melalui komentar, direct message, Story, dan polling; serta word of mouth melalui tag, mention, dan repost unggahan konsumen. Strategi tersebut mendukung brand recognition dan brand recall mahasiswa, meskipun posisi top of mind belum tercapai secara merata. Oleh karena itu, konsistensi publikasi konten, respons terhadap konsumen, dan penguatan interaksi digital perlu ditingkatkan agar kesadaran merek EIGER semakin kuat.

title: Keadilan dan Integritas Hukum pada Masa Pemerintahan Harun al-Rasyid
abstractText: Dinasti Abbasiyah, khususnya di masa Khalifah Harun ar-Rasyid, merupakan puncak kejayaan peradaban Islam yang mencatat banyak kemajuan gemilang. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kualitatif dengan pendekatan historis untuk mengkaji peradaban Dinasti Abbasiyah pada masa pemerintahan Harun ar-Rasyid. Data diperoleh melalui studi pustaka dan dianalisis menggunakan analisis isi untuk mengungkap peran kepemimpinan serta dinamika sosial-politik dalam mendorong kemajuan ilmu pengetahuan, budaya, dan pemerintahan Dinasti Abbasiyah. Hasil pembahasan menunjukkan bahwa pemerintahan Harun ar-Rasyid pada masa Dinasti Abbasiyah merupakan puncak kejayaan Islam, ditandai dengan kemajuan di bidang politik, ekonomi, hukum, pendidikan, dan ilmu pengetahuan. Ia membangun birokrasi modern, memperkuat militer, menjadikan Baghdad pusat peradaban, serta mendirikan Baitul Hikmah sebagai pusat ilmu. Pemerintahannya inklusif dan adil, dengan penegakan hukum yang tegas dan dukungan terhadap kebebasan berpikir. Masa ini dikenal sebagai era keemasan Islam, ditandai dengan toleransi tinggi dan kontribusi besar para imam mazhab dalam pengembangan hukum Islam.

Research on “Three Entries” Ideological and Political Curriculum Integration: A Case Study of English Writing Course
abstractText: This study carried out a one semester comparative teaching experiment of curriculum ideological political education for second year English teacher majors in ZW University of China. Guided by the Production Oriented Approach (POA), the experiment integrated socialist core values into the whole process blended teaching of English Writing. The experimental group adopted an integrated online offline teaching design embedded with curriculum ideological political elements, while the control group received conventional writing instruction without special ideological political interventions. Multiple data sources including unified final examination papers, standardized questionnaires and semi structured individual & group interviews were adopted. Three core dimensions, namely learning motivation, value cognition improvement, and overall writing academic performance, were measured for effect evaluation. The experimental results demonstrated that the experimental group achieved statistically significant improvements across all three dimensions. Students’ comprehension of Chinese discourse, cross cultural critical thinking competence, and mission awareness to tell Chinese stories in English were notably enhanced. In contrast, no statistically significant changes were observed among the control group regarding learning initiative, value cognition or writing achievements. This experiment verifies that well integrated ideological political education in English writing courses can effectively stimulate students’ intrinsic learning drive, improve professional academic output and shape sound ideals, beliefs and value stances. It provides replicable practical cases and empirical evidence for curriculum ideological political reform for foreign language majors in higher education.

title: Mapping Lacrosse Injury and Sports Medicine Research
abstractText: Background Lacrosse research spans orthopedic injury, concussion, prevention, and sports science. This study characterized publication, citation, and collaboration patterns in a search-defined literature. Methods Web of Science records exported on July 22, 2026, were analyzed. Of 458 unique retrieved records, 24 clearly out-of-scope records were excluded. The primary corpus required lacrosse in the title, abstract, or author keywords, yielding 388 records. A broader 434-record corpus included additional records linked only through Keywords Plus. Indicators were recalculated from the full-record export. Results The primary corpus spanned 1987–2026, contained 141 source-title labels, and accumulated 14,987 citations (mean, 38.63; h-index, 61). Of the records, 235 (60.6%) were dated 2017–2026; 2026 was incomplete. American Journal of Sports Medicine and Journal of Athletic Training each contributed 44 records. Sport Sciences and Orthopedics were assigned to 275 (70.9%) and 120 (30.9%) records, respectively. An explicit USA address label occurred in 343 records (88.4%). Injury, concussion, and epidemiology were the most frequent normalized keywords. The broader sensitivity analysis retained concussion and epidemiology among its leading terms. Conclusions This literature connects lacrosse injury research with broader sports medicine and is concentrated in US-affiliated publications. Concussion and epidemiology are prominent, but bibliometric patterns do not establish clinical evidence quality or quantify treatment-related research gaps.

title: Preferensi Konsumen terhadap Teh Celup Berdasarkan Atribut Produk: A Literature Review
abstractText: Consumer preferences for tea bags are influenced by various product attributes, including sensory and non-sensory attributes. This literature review aims to identify product attributes related to consumer preferences, compare the attributes considered by consumers based on previous studies, and identify the product attributes most frequently found in studies on consumer preferences for tea bags. This review uses a descriptive qualitative approach through a literature review of eight scientific journal articles published between 2016 and 2025. Previous studies were compared based on the product attributes examined and consumer preferences identified in each study. The results show that the attributes considered by consumers include taste, aroma, color, price, brand, packaging, quantity, size, and practicality. These attributes are classified into sensory attributes, namely taste, aroma, and color, and non-sensory attributes, namely packaging, price, brand, quantity, size, and practicality. Based on the frequency of occurrence, taste was the most frequently identified attribute, appearing in all eight studies, followed by packaging, price, aroma, color, brand, quantity, size, and practicality. These findings indicate that consumer preferences for tea bags are formed through a combination of sensory and non-sensory attributes, with taste being the attribute most consistently preferred by consumers in previous studies.

title: Interpersonal Relationships in the Poem “Kafānī Aẓillu bi Huḍnihā” by Fadwa Tuqan
abstractText: This study is a descriptive qualitative research aimed at analyzing the symbolic attachment between the lyrical subject and Palestine in Fadwa Tuqan’s poem titled “Kafānī Aẓillu bi Huḍnihā” using John Bowlby’s attachment theory. The primary data consists of the poem “Kafānī Aẓillu bi Ḥuḍnihā” by Fadwa Tuqan. In contrast, the secondary data includes books, news articles, journal articles, and theoretical literature related to Palestine, Attachment Theory, and the historical-social context. Data were collected through triangulation (data collection, reduction, and display) and analyzed using content analysis with a heuristic-hermeneutic approach. The interpersonal relationship between people and place is represented through the Palestinian people’s affective attachment to the land of Palestine, expressed through the word “حُضْنِ,” which means “the homeland as a mother’s embrace. The research findings indicate the presence of attachment concepts from John Bowlby’s theory divided into six concepts (Safe Haven, Secure Base, Internal Working Model, Continuity of Attachment, Intergenerational Attachment, and Enduring Attachment) as derived from the symbols used in the poem “Kafānī Aẓillu bi Huḍnihā,”. This study contributes to the understanding of literature as a social tool that plays a dynamic role in society by fostering a literate awareness that brings comfort to fellow human beings.

STREET ADDRESSING AND STREET RENAMING IN YANTALA (NIAMEY, NIGER): A GIS TO INVENTORY PUBLIC GREEN SPACES AND TRACK RENAMED STREETS
abstractText: Since 2023, Niamey has been renaming some of its streets and squares, while its addressing system still relies on a 2004 plan. This study examines how a geographic information system can, at the neighbourhood level, both inventory public green spaces and track street renaming. A database of six feature classes, designed in ArcGIS, stores for each street its 2004 code, former name, and new name. It is shared in KML format. The September 2026 survey in Yantala covered the 21 segments of named streets, 11 new names, the neighbourhood’s 3 public green spaces and 15 control points; seven municipal officers tested the tool. No street-name sign has ever been installed, and no new name is displayed. Six of the 11 new names relate to arts and culture; 2 refer to women. Green spaces cover 3,436 m², about 0.04 m² per inhabitant, and the Château I garden has lost 82% of its area to a restaurant. The positional error (RMSE) is 0.19 m. With the tool, the officers completed all 21 tasks; with the current method, only 9. The mean usability score is 92.9/100. The GIS is currently the only medium in which codes, former names, and new names coexist; it can serve as a common reference for municipal services.

title: Optimalisasi Budidaya dan Hilirisasi Tanaman Obat Keluarga (DISANTARA) untuk Meningkatkan Kesehatan dan Ekonomi Masyarakat Desa Wates secara Berkelanjutan
abstractText: Community health and economy are two interrelated aspects of sustainable regional development. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of the Optimization of Cultivation and Downstreaming of Family Medicinal Plants (DISANTARA) program in Wates Village, Undaan District, Kudus Regency, in improving community health and economy sustainably. This study employed an exploratory sequential mixed methods approach combined with a qualitative descriptive method based on Participatory Action Research (PAR). Secondary quantitative data related to health and economic indicators were analyzed using descriptive statistics, while qualitative data from Focus Group Discussions, participatory observation, and in-depth interviews were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model. The results showed that the majority of Wates Village residents work as farmers (52%), and the most common health complaint was respiratory disorders (62%). The DISANTARA program successfully established the SAHARA (Healthy and Natural Herbal Center) institution consisting of four working divisions, revitalized the Sustainable Food Yard into a Seed House as a center for TOGA cultivation, and produced six downstream herbal products, namely SABUYA, SABULAWA, JA Candy, SERUAS Tea, KUNIRA, and KENCARA. The integration of cultivation, education, institutional strengthening, and product downstreaming proved effective in supporting improved health and economic independence of the community. This study implies the need for institutional strengthening, product legality, and market network development to sustain and expand the program's impact.

Chronic systemic capillary leak syndrome with monoclonal kappa light chain gammopathy responsive to intravenous immunoglobulin: a case report
abstractText: Abstract Background Systemic capillary leak syndrome (SCLS) is a rare disorder characterized by transient plasma extravasation due to endothelial barrier dysfunction. It may occur idiopathically (ISCLS) or in association with monoclonal gammopathy (MG-CLS), a form also known as Clarkson’s disease. Case presentation We describe a 39-year-old woman with a 15-year history of episodic, symmetric limb edema and profuse sweating, unresponsive to antihistamines or corticosteroids over several years. Episodes were chronic and lacked hypotension or pruritus. Laboratory workup revealed monoclonal kappa light chain gammopathy and borderline hemoconcentration. Monthly high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG, 2 g/kg) was initiated. Improvement was noted by the fourth infusion, with complete resolution of swelling and marked reduction in sweating after five months of therapy. IVIG was well tolerated apart from mild infusion-related headache. Conclusions This case illustrates that MG-CLS may present as a chronic disorder without the classic triad and may respond favorably to IVIG. In selected patients with mild or atypical presentations, a therapeutic trial of IVIG may be considered.

title: Molecular Identification, Diversity, and Antifungal Susceptibility of Clinical Yeasts Associated with Human Skin Spots
abstractText: Fungi associated with different parts of human body and cause approximately a million deaths and a billion superficial infections annually. That need to identify their causes and the optimum antifungal treatments. In this work, biodiversity, morphology and molecular identification using rDNA ITS, and antifungal susceptibility of isolated fungal yeasts associated with collected samples from 30 patients’ skin spots from different regions in Iraq have been investigated. Phenotypic and molecular identification, and a phylogenetic tree were utilized to assess yeasts to species level and their biodiversity. Furthermore, the efficacy of three certain antifungal agents for detected dermophyte fungi was tested. The results in this study revealed the association of the ascomycetous yeasts such as Candida intermedia (12 isolates) and Candida sp. (9 isolates) and basidiomycetous yeasts; Naganishia diffluens (25 isolates), Rhodotorula glutinis (4 isolates), Rhodotorula diobovata (one isolates), Rhodotorula mucilaginosa (one isolates), and Filobasidium magnum (3 isolates) with skin spots. Based on available data, this is the first record of all detected yeast species associated with skin spots in Iraq except R. mucilaginosa. Biodiversity of yeasts revealed that Naganishia diffluens and Candida intermedia were predominant species and the highest diversity across the patients based on diversity indices. Antifungal susceptibility test showed that R. mucilaginosa was resistant to two of three tested antifungals. It is concluded most yeast species were recorded for the first time from the skin spots in Iraq with variant Antifungal susceptibility of three yeast species. These findings could provide insight to fungi associated with skin spots and selecting the optimum antifungals.

One-Pot Synthesis of Oxidation-Resistant Silica-Coated Iron Nanoparticles via Ultrasonically Assisted Citrate Modification
abstractText: Abstract This study presents a facile, one-pot aqueous coating strategy to synthesize oxidation-resistant silica-coated iron (Fe/SiO2) core–shell nanoparticles under ambient conditions. Citrate-mediated reduction produced metallic Fe cores, with citrate ions and a thin native surface oxide layer acting as interfacial modifiers that promote SiO2 nucleation and eliminate the need for intermediate washing. Ultrasonication-assisted SiO2 encapsulation via a sol–gel process yielded Fe/SiO2 nanoparticles comprising a metallic Fe core (50.4 ± 15.1 nm in diameter) and a SiO2 shell (14.1 nm thick), as confirmed by transmission electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. Magnetic measurements demonstrated that the saturation magnetization of bare Fe nanoparticles decreased from 105.9 to 39.7 emu g–1 after 72 h in water owing to oxidation, whereas that of Fe/SiO2 nanoparticles remained at 84.6 emu g–1 compared with an initial value of 86.4 emu g–1. X-ray diffraction confirmed the preservation of the metallic α-Fe (body-centered cubic) phase, demonstrating that the SiO2 shell served as an effective diffusion barrier against oxidation. By providing a facile and eco-friendly route to protect metallic nanomaterials robustly, this study opens new avenues for their practical applications in advanced magnetic sensors, biosensors, catalysis, and magnetic separation.

Combined application of Azospirillum brasilense and humic acid improves growth, physiology and yield of wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) under tillering-stage drought stress
abstractText: Abstract Drought at the tillering stage is one of the most damaging abiotic constraints to wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) production in arid and semi-arid cropping systems. A field experiment was conducted to evaluate whether the plant growth-promoting rhizobacterium Azospirillum brasilense and the organic soil amendment humic acid, applied singly or in combination, could mitigate the adverse effects of drought stress imposed at the tillering stage. The experiment was laid out in a randomized complete block design with eight treatments and three replications: an untreated control, sole A. brasilense , sole humic acid, and their combination, each evaluated under well-watered and drought-stressed conditions. Drought stress was initiated at tillering (25 days after sowing) by withholding the first irrigation and was maintained for 21 days, after which normal irrigation resumed. Drought stress significantly ( p < 0.01) reduced all measured growth, physiological and yield attributes relative to the well-watered control. Sole application of A. brasilense or humic acid partially alleviated these reductions, but the combined treatment consistently produced the most favorable outcome under both water regimes. Under well-watered conditions, the combined treatment increased plant height, spike length, spikelets per spike, 1000-grain weight, grain yield and biological yield by 13.2, 25.4, 9.9, 10.5, 0.9 and 1.8%, respectively, relative to the untreated control, and it also recorded the highest stomatal conductance, crop growth rate, relative water content and leaf area index. Under drought, the combined treatment (T7) improved grain and biological yieldrelative to the drought control (T4), and its drought susceptibility index for grain yield (0.55) was less than half that of the untreated pairing (1.29), indicating markedly improved drought tolerance. These results indicate that A. brasilense and humic acid act in a complementary manner, whereby microbial phytohormone and nitrogen-fixation activity are reinforced by the water- and nutrient-retention properties of humic acid, and that their combined field application is a practical, low-cost strategy for sustaining wheat productivity under water-limited conditions. Governing the Capability-Accountability Gap through Global Capability Centres as Regulatory Nodes in the Gulf
abstractText: Global Capability Centres (GCCs), wholly-owned “captive” units through which multinational enterprises internalise offshore delivery, have migrated from cost-driven back offices toward research, engineering, artificial-intelligence (AI) development, cybersecurity and financial-control functions of global consequence. This article theorises the legal consequences of that migration in the Gulf, where the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia have simultaneously constructed ambitious data- and AI-governance architectures. Its central and integrating claim is that when a GCC accumulates functional and technological capability faster than it acquires corresponding decision authority, legal responsibility and answerability, a Capability-Accountability Asymmetry emerges, producing a Regulatory Accountability Gap (RAG), a divergence between where consequential activity is performed and where legal answerability is located. The article makes four connected contributions. First, it develops the asymmetry into a Four-A model (capability, authority, responsibility, accountability) and operationalises the RAG through a diagnostic matrix and a set of threshold conditions, so that the gap becomes an analytical construct rather than a metaphor. Second, it offers a four-layer “Accountability Stack” (structural, operational, decision and behavioural) as a diagnostic instrument and applies it to a worked case. Third, it advances a four-stage “Regulatory Maturity Curve” on which RAG intensity rises during capability expansion and may fall as authority is re-allocated. Fourth, it reframes the “copy-paste” compliance error as Regulatory Translation Failure, grounded in legal-transplant theory, and reads the Saudi and Emirati regimes as two institutional solutions, centralised regulatory translation and polycentric regulatory reconciliation, to the same problem. Drawing on legal-pluralism, transplant, regulatory-intermediary and accountability scholarship and on doctrinal analysis of the relevant Gulf instruments, it conceptualises mature GCCs as sites of regulatory translation and co-production, and closes with boundary conditions, limitations and an agenda for empirical research.

In October, conservation work was carried out using stone slabs found within the pond in order to protect the structural features such as the steps and embankments. This research is conducted with the aim of examining whether the content of the inscription can contribute to understanding the functional usage of the pond. Based on the paleographic features of the script, the discovered inscription can be dated approximately to the 3rd century CE, and it consists of four lines of writing. Although the information revealed is limited, it can be concluded that these findings will be highly significant for future studies related to the history of Abhayagiri.

abstractText: Abstract The digital transformation of the construction industry has positioned Building Information Modeling as a key approach for improving collaboration, productivity, project quality, and lifecycle management. However, its adoption in Morocco remains limited and fragmented despite the country’s expanding infrastructure program. This systematic review assesses the current state of Building Information Modeling adoption in Morocco, identifies the principal barriers and enabling factors, and proposes a context-specific strategy for wider implementation. Literature published between 2010 and 2025 was identified through Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect and was complemented by a documentary analysis of Moroccan regulations, institutional reports, professional initiatives, educational programs, and documented implementation activities. The evidence was synthesized narratively and supported by comparative policy benchmarking involving the United Kingdom, Singapore, France, the United Arab Emirates, Brazil, and South Africa. The findings indicate that adoption in Morocco is constrained by the absence of a national mandate, harmonized standards, institutional coordination, and legal recognition of digital information deliverables. Additional barriers include limited digital maturity among small and medium-sized enterprises, high implementation costs, shortages of qualified professionals, cultural resistance, interoperability difficulties, and unequal digital infrastructure. Nevertheless, major infrastructure investments, growing academic interest, private-sector initiatives, an emerging digitally skilled workforce, and proximity to European markets provide favorable conditions for development. Based on the synthesized evidence, a phased national roadmap for 2025–2035 is proposed, encompassing governance and standardization, pilot implementation, professional training, progressive requirements for public projects, financial support, and integration into higher education. Coordinated action among public authorities, professional organizations, universities, and industry is essential for achieving sustainable digital transformation and strengthening the regional competitiveness of Morocco’s construction sector.

abstractText: In a dynamic cellular manufacturing system (D-CMS), the production-cell capacity, described by the two parameters LP (minimum number of machines per cell) and CL (maximum number of machines per cell), exerts a decisive influence on the optimal solutions of a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model aimed at minimizing the cellular load variation. Starting from two experiments gathering configurations solved by the LINGO solver (50 instances per configuration), this paper proposes an enriched sensitivity analysis of the impact of the parameters LP and CL. We show that the slack margin Δ = CL − LP is strongly correlated with the optimal value, but that this correlation crucially depends on the experimental protocol: when CL is held fixed and LP varies, the relationship becomes quasi-deterministic (R² ≥ 0.98), whereas when LP and CL are randomly chosen, the coefficient of determination drops to about 0.46. We also identify the profitability thresholds S⋆ below which the company realizes profits (limited machine sales) and beyond which it incurs losses (massive machine sales). The results show that in-house production systematically prevails over subcontracting whenever capacity allows, and that keeping the cell slack below the threshold S⋆ is a necessary condition to avoid losses. These results constitute a significant deepening of the reference model previously published in Statistics, Optimization and Information Computing (see Yao K. Adrien et al., 2025), and provide industrial decision makers with operational pre-sizing rules for the cell capacity.

Robust multi-weather UAV small object detection framework with complex entropy-aware and wavelet convolution
abstractText: Abstract In adverse weather conditions such as fog, haze, rain, and snow, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) small object detection faces decreased accuracy due to reduced image quality and blurred object features, which seriously affects the reliability of low-altitude detection tasks. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a robust multi-weather UAV small object detection framework based on unsupervised domain adaptation with a teacher-student self-training paradigm. The proposed framework introduces complex entropy-aware attention and wavelet convolution to enhance target representation under severe weather degradation. Aiming at the domain distribution differences in multi-weather scenarios, the framework alleviates such differences through more robust category-level prototype matching and global statistical characteristic learning based on DATR (domain adaptive detection transformer model). First, to alleviate feature uncertainty introduced by adverse weather noise, we design a complex entropy-aware attention mechanism that estimates channel-wise Shannon entropy and assigns adaptive weights according to feature information concentration. Instead of simply emphasizing uncertain responses, the proposed mechanism suppresses high-entropy ambiguous features while preserving low-entropy discriminative representations that remain more reliable under weather-induced degradation. Next, to solve the limitations of traditional convolution in capturing the global context of small objects and distinguishing objects from noise, we propose to use wavelet convolution to leverage frequency-domain multi-scale decomposition and large receptive fields, strengthening the capture of global context for small objects and improving the distinction between objects and noise through frequency filtering. Finally, to further improve the stability of teacher model evolution under cross-weather domain shifts, we design a grouped EMA (exponential moving average) strategy. Unlike conventional Mean Teacher or BYOL frameworks that employ a globally fixed decay coefficient, the proposed strategy dynamically adjusts grouped parameter updating rates according to feature adaptation requirements, providing a more flexible optimization trajectory for domain adaptation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves UAV small object detection performance under several adverse weather domain-shift scenarios, while showing promising robustness against weather-induced feature degradation.

Jet-streak forcing and deep moisture transport during the 7 March 2025 record rainfall in Bahía Blanca, Argentina
abstractText: Bahía Blanca (38.7°S, 62.2°W) experienced an unprecedented rainfall event on 7 March 2025, officially documented by the Servicio Meteorológico Nacional (SMN) as a historical record with an estimated return period exceeding 100 years. This study provides an observationally based diagnosis of the event, testing the hypothesis that record precipitation resulted from the coupling between upper-level jet-streak-associated divergence, deep ascent and exceptional moisture transport. We combine integrated multi-satellite retrievals for global precipitation measurement (IMERG) satellite precipitation with ERA5 (fifth generation ECMWF (European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts) atmospheric reanalysis) reanalysis fields and adopt event-consistent daily metrics (24-h windows) to characterise the dynamical and thermodynamical environment. IMERG reveals a spatially organised precipitation footprint co-located with a persistent corridor of enhanced integrated vapour transport (IVT) toward south-eastern Buenos Aires Province. Over the upstream region of Bahía Blanca, upper-level diagnostics show an anomalous jet-streak configuration at 200 hPa (along-flow acceleration percentile 99.3%) concurrent with extremely rare divergence at 200 hPa (percentile 99.8%) and exceptionally strong deep ascent (minimum ω daily metric, percentile 99.9%). Vertical diagnostics indicate that moisture transport was not confined to the boundary layer: layer-integrated fluxes show substantial contributions from mid-to-upper tropospheric levels (700–300 hPa) consistent with a deep warm conveyor belt like moist airstream during the event window. Together, the results support a proximal mechanism in which an anomalous upper-level jet-streak induced extreme divergence and deep ascent that, when coupled with record-level moisture transport, produced the observed catastrophic rainfall.

title: Kualitas Pelayanan, Fasilitas, dan Kompetensi Petugas sebagai Prediktor Kepuasan Masyarakat pada Layanan e-KTP di Kota Samarinda
abstractText: Kepuasan masyarakat merupakan indikator utama kinerja pelayanan publik, tetapi belum jelas apakah fasilitas fisik berkontribusi terhadap kepuasan di luar proses layanan dan petugas ketika warga tidak dapat memilih penyedia layanan lain. Penelitian ini menguji apakah kualitas pelayanan, fasilitas pelayanan, dan kompetensi petugas berasosiasi dengan kepuasan masyarakat pada layanan Kartu Tanda Penduduk elektronik (e-KTP) di Dinas Kependudukan dan Pencatatan Sipil Kota Samarinda, Indonesia, serta apakah fasilitas masih berkontribusi secara unik setelah kedua variabel lainnya dikendalikan. Survei potong lintang yang bersifat eksplanatori-prediktif dilakukan pada Juli 2026 terhadap 100 pengguna layanan yang dipilih melalui accidental sampling. Instrumen berupa kuesioner 17 butir berskala Likert lima tingkat, dengan korelasi butir-total terkoreksi 0,321–0,615 dan koefisien Cronbach’s alpha 0,680–0,693. Data dianalisis dengan regresi linear berganda menggunakan IBM SPSS 25 setelah uji asumsi klasik. Kualitas pelayanan (β = 0,215; p = 0,025) dan kompetensi petugas (β = 0,300; p = 0,009) berasosiasi positif dan signifikan dengan kepuasan, sedangkan fasilitas tidak (β = 0,020; p = 0,861). Secara simultan, ketiga variabel berasosiasi signifikan dengan kepuasan (F = 5,626; p = 0,001) dan menjelaskan 15,0% variasinya (R² terkoreksi = 0,123). Fasilitas berkorelasi kuat dengan kompetensi petugas (r = 0,538), sehingga keduanya sulit dipisahkan secara empiris. Kepuasan dengan demikian tampak lebih erat kaitannya dengan penyampaian layanan dan kemampuan petugas daripada fasilitas fisik, meskipun inferensi kausal tidak dapat dilakukan.

HallucinationNerd: A Framework and Tool to Detect Hallucinations and Unsupported Claims
abstractText: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic systems, and human authors produce text with inline citations, but the cited sources do not always support the claims attributed to them. We present HallucinationNerd, a modular citation-verification engine that decomposes text into atomic claims, retrieves relevant passages from each cited source, and determines whether the source supports the claim. In addition, HallucinationNerd identifies claims that carry no citation and searches user-approved databases to find or refute supporting evidence for them. The system handles five common citation formats, operates on PDFs, web pages, and plain text, and produces per-claim verdicts with evidence pointers. The underlying algorithm mixes parsing (to identify claim–citation pairs), overlapped chunking, stopword elimination, and AI-based semantic comparison. In head-to-head comparison on the same data, HallucinationNerd substantially outperforms (by about 20% in F1 score) state-of-the-art systems on accuracy and precision on a benchmark built from research papers. HallucinationNerd can also be used to verify the output of other AI systems. For example, we audited a set of outputs of Scholar GPT, a publicly available scholarly research agent. In that sample at least, its citations were faithful to the cited sources.
